jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Austria has not yet passed a law implementing the EU AI Act or designated its market surveillance authorities (as of October 2026); the AI Act applies directly through the EU layer. Its national framework is the federal AI strategy AIM AT 2030 (2021) with the 2024 implementation plan, Council of Ministers decisions on an AI measures package (2023), the Digital Austria Act and its 2.0 update, and a 2026 public-sector AI initiative, together with AI guidelines and practice guides for the public service. A 2024 law created an AI Service Desk and an AI Advisory Board at the regulator RTR; the data protection authority has issued an AI FAQ and circulars on the GDPR and the AI Act, and RTR has published guidance on labelling AI content in the media. Several laws carry explicit AI provisions: a 2026 school law makes computer science and AI a compulsory subject from 2027, higher-education law treats misuse of AI as academic misconduct, anti-money-laundering law allows AI-based transaction monitoring, and data protection law limits automated decisions in law enforcement. Vienna has an AI strategy and staff guidance on generative AI, and Upper Austria passed the first Land law with AI provisions (2025).
lead_institutions: Austrian Regulatory Authority for Broadcasting and Telecommunications (AI Service Desk)
Federal Ministry for Innovation, Mobility and Infrastructure
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 11 October 2026, covering federal laws, government and ministries, regulators and the Länder of Vienna, Upper Austria and Styria, searched in German and English, with EU instruments such as the AI Act recorded in the EU file. Several items are pending, including the Financial Market Authority's AI material, the national AI Act implementation law, the amendment allowing fully automated administrative decisions and a new AI strategy announced for 2027, so these are listed as leads to check later.

instruments.summary: Austria's first national AI strategy, jointly prepared by the climate/innovation and the digital/economy ministries, with three aims: AI for the common good on the basis of fundamental rights and European values, positioning Austria as an AI research and innovation location, and securing competitiveness. It is organised in two pillars, 'trustworthy AI' (including ethics, legal framework, security, standards, public administration and skills) and 'creating an AI ecosystem', across 13 fields of action, and an annex sets out 11 application fields (e.g. climate, energy, industry, health, education, law); strategy and annex together contain 91 measures. It states that administrative decisions with direct and significant effects on people may be machine-supported but not taken by machines.

instruments.summary: Vienna's AI strategy, a sub-strategy of the Digitale Agenda 2030, anchors the City administration's use of AI in 'digital humanism' and sets three strategic thrusts: for the digital city (use-case evaluation, new AI services, process automation), for the city administration (guidelines for ethical, transparent and risk-based AI use in line with the AI Act, a voluntary commitment to transparency on generative AI, a mandatory central electronic register of all AI applications, steering of AI in the City's IT governance, AI competence building) and for society and economy (technology assessment, cooperation, open AI models and training data). It is addressed to all departments of the City of Vienna.

The compass states it deliberately is not a detailed Richtlinie and is reviewed and updated as needed.
instruments.summary: Staff guidance for employees of the Vienna city administration on using generative AI tools: official use of freely available generative AI tools is permitted, subject to existing decrees on data protection, IT security and official communication, and to principles of legality, economy and ethics. Only public data may be entered into freely available internet tools, while the City's internal 'Wien KI-Plattform' may, on the basis of a data-protection impact assessment, temporarily receive data classified 'restricted' or 'confidential'; other AI applications follow the approval process under the AI Act. Staff remain responsible for AI-generated content, must label AI-generated texts and images externally with a set disclosure sentence, and should check outputs for hallucinations and deepfakes.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Mandatory-in-practice rules for generative AI use in the Magistrat of Vienna, including a labelling duty for AI-generated content.

instruments.current_status: Upper Austrian state law LGBl. Nr. 46/2025 (government bill Beilage 1016/2024, committee report Beilage 1134/2025, 36th Landtag session), issued 12 June 2025 and in force from 13 June 2025 under § 7, which provides that it enters into force at the end of the day of its promulgation.
instruments.summary: Upper Austrian Land law promoting transparent and traceable use of AI systems and automated decision-making by the Oö. Landtag, Land authorities and departments, municipalities and other public-law bodies in the Land's competence. It authorises these bodies to take part in AI regulatory sandboxes under Art. 57 of the EU AI Act and to process personal data (including special categories) to develop, train, validate, test and operate AI systems that are not prohibited or high-risk, subject to necessity, data-quality and documentation duties. It permits fully automated decisions by non-AI IT for services provided under private law, with reasoning, labelling as automated, official signature, pre-deployment testing, documentation of the logic and algorithms, and logging requirements.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: One of the first Austrian Land laws with explicit AI provisions: AI sandbox participation, legal basis for AI training data in the administration, and safeguards for automated decisions.

organizations.name: Austrian Council on Robotics and Artificial Intelligence

organizations.name: National Council

organizations.name: Federal Ministry of Education

Method note (original): Deep review completed on 11 October 2026, covering federal laws and regulations, the federal government and ministries, the data protection authority, RTR, KommAustria and the competition authority, and the Länder of Vienna, Upper Austria and Styria.
